$$
\{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)+2={X}_{1}(s)+\frac{3}{s} \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-1=-{X}_{1}(s)+3{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\},$ and we have used the fact that $L\{1\}=\frac{1}{s}.$

Now, solving the first equation for ${X}_{1}(s),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)+2 & ={X}_{1}(s)+\frac{3}{s} \\ (s-1){X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{3}{s}-2 \\ (s-1){X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{3-2s}{s} \\ {X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{3-2s}{s(s-1)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this in the second equation and solving for ${X}_{2}(s),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}s{X}_{2}(s)-1 & =-{X}_{1}(s)+3{X}_{2}(s) \\ (s-3){X}_{2}(s) & =1-{X}_{1}(s) \\ (s-3){X}_{2}(s) & =1-(\frac{3-2s}{s(s-1)}) \\ (s-3){X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{s(s-1)-3+2s}{s(s-1)} \\ (s-3){X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{{s}^{2}-s-3+2s}{s(s-1)} \\ (s-3){X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{{s}^{2}+s-3}{s(s-1)} \\ {X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{{s}^{2}+s-3}{s(s-1)(s-3)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution of the new system  in terms of parameter $s$ is 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{3-2s}{s(s-1)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{{s}^{2}+s-3}{s(s-1)(s-3)}.
$$
